rektion: etw. für + Adj. / als + Adj./Akk. erachten (für notwendig, als sinnvoll erachten); gehoben
definition_de: etwas nach eigenem Urteil für etwas halten, meist gehoben oder formell (etwas für notwendig, sinnvoll, angemessen erachten; meines Erachtens = meiner Meinung nach)
example_de: Der Mechaniker erachtete eine Reparatur des völlig verrosteten Autos nicht mehr für sinnvoll.
example_en: The mechanic no longer considered repairing the completely rusted car worthwhile.
visual_idea: Collocation 'etw. (nicht) für sinnvoll erachten': an expert gives his judgement on something clearly visible. A mechanic shaking his head next to a hopelessly rusted car, the owner looking crestfallen, makes the verdict obvious and a little funny. Beat 'die Ärztin erachtet eine Operation für notwendig' (the X-ray is small, the scene reads as zeigen/erklären) and 'die Jury erachtet seinen Kuchen als den besten' (reads as bewerten/probieren).
image_prompt: a gray-haired mechanic in blue overalls standing beside a small old car that is completely covered in brown rust with holes in the doors and a sagging bumper, he shakes his head with a regretful face and spreads his hands, the young owner stands next to him looking crestfallen, inside a bright car repair workshop with a hydraulic lift and tool walls, plain blank walls, medium-wide shot
negative_prompt: text, letters, watermark, signature, caption, blurry, extra fingers, deformed hands, cluttered background, multiple panels, logos, license plate
video_prompt: in a bright car workshop, a gray-haired mechanic in blue overalls walks slowly around a completely rusted small old car, taps the rusty door, then turns to the young owner, shakes his head and spreads his hands regretfully while the owner's face falls; static camera
